proposal:
SCOPE. Nothing was executed; all traces are by hand from the supplied code. No all-CNF bound is claimed.

1. AUDIT OF PINNED CODE. compression._verify_certificate builds blocks from every original clause, confines each used form to its block mask, compares all 2^w local points and checks every entry of P*L=I, giving F(x)=Q(Px) with P surjective. Work caps are tested before each block loop. core_refutation drops only input clauses (subset gate) and accepts only a 2-SAT-UNSAT quotient; run_counting returns early only on UNSAT. I find no soundness defect. The cost defect is that step() calls refute at every node: in the 00069 receipt IALH took 3.50 of 3.61 s for 3 refutations. Exact gate (STAR): if a tuple c and its w neighbours c+e_i all survive UP, their differences generate Z^w, so the window yields neither a row nor an empty table. Skipping the remaining 2^w-w-1 UP runs and the HNF leaves every certificate unchanged, provided budget accounting is kept identical. Corollary: a window gives rows only if dead tuples dominate survivors, which needs at least ceil(2^w/(w+1)) dead tuples (6 for w=5).

2. MODULE-SPLIT (sound restricted rule). Fix a variable set M. Split each clause touching M as L u C, where L is its literals on M and C is the context. Group by context; G_C is the set of local parts. Suppose only two distinct families G1, G2 occur (syntactic equality suffices), with context sets C1, C2, and M occurs nowhere else. Put Phi_i = AND of C_i, R = remaining clauses, and s1, s2, s12 = satisfiability of G1, G2, G1^G2. Then F = (G1(x) v Phi1(z)) ^ (G2(x) v Phi2(z)) ^ R(z), and
EXISTS x F == R ^ [ s12 v (s1 ^ Phi2) v (s2 ^ Phi1) v (Phi1 ^ Phi2) ].
Cases:
- s12 true: delete all M-clauses.
- s1, s2 true, s12 false: Q = R + {p v C : C in C1} + {-p v C : C in C2}, p fresh. Lift with stored witnesses x1 |= G1 (p=1) and x2 |= G2 (p=0).
- G_i unsatisfiable: keep the contexts C_i as clauses and delete the other family's clauses (keep both if both are unsatisfiable).
Polarity and linearity are irrelevant. OR/AND twins, XOR pairs and any t-ary gate with a complementary family are instances. G2 need not equal not-G1, so no dualization check is needed, only local SAT on M. |M|=1 is ordinary DP with no gain. For m families: EXISTS x F == R ^ OR over maximal satisfiable subfamilies S of AND_{i not in S} Phi_i.

3. NEON58 BY HAND, raw 20-variable input, arity 2 only.
- {17,18}: 12 negative contexts carry {(-17,18),(17,-18)} and 6 positive contexts carry {(17,18),(-17,-18)}. The conjunction is UNSAT by a 4-row table, so merge to p. Same for {13,14}, {15,16}, {19,20}.
- OR-type, e.g. {1,9}: G1={(1,9)}, G2={(-1),(-9)}. Likewise the other seven pairs, giving P1..P4 and Q1..Q4.
- AND-type on side A: {P1,P2} has G1={(P1),(P2)} over contexts {Qj} and G2={(-P1,-P2)} over context {-P3,-P4}. Two more merges leave the unit (-P) and (P v Qj). UP forces every Qj and falsifies (-Q1,-Q2,-Q3,-Q4).
Total: 15 merges, no branching, no IALH.
One larger step also exists. For M={1,3,5,7,9,11,13,14,17,18} the six positive contexts {2,10}, {4,12}, {6,15,16}, {6,-15,-16}, {8,19,20}, {8,-19,-20} share the same six local clauses (I checked the 6x6 rectangle clause by clause), and the 36 negative clauses have empty context.

4. TOTAL WORK. Gate: apply only if 2(|G1|+|G2|)+|Q| < |F|, counted in literal occurrences. Then any recursion tree has at most 2|F| nodes and total leaf size at most |F|. Arity-t discovery takes t-subsets of clause supports as candidates, at most |F|*w^(t-1) of them. Each is tested by one sort, O(|F| log|F|) comparisons of O(log n)-bit ids, and local SAT is a 2^t table. The certificate is the local tables plus two witnesses, the same shape as the Lean-checked block rule. For fixed t the factoring overhead is polynomial in encoded bits. Leaves go to the existing solver and their work is NOT bounded.

5. INDEPENDENT TEST PREDICTIONS (unimplemented, so fixture is null).
(a) Canonical fixture: UNSAT with 0 branch nodes, order-independent, at most 15 merges at t=2.
(b) Pigeonhole h=4,5: rule inert. A same-pigeon pair gives three families (x v y), {-x}, {-y} with three maximal satisfiable subfamilies and no size gain. Timings should be unchanged.
(c) Add clause [1,2,17] to the fixture: a third family appears for {17,18} and the exact rule stalls on that pair. An UNSAT-only variant that drops minority-family clauses (sound as a core) should still refute.
(d) STAR: identical statuses, peaks and certificates on all existing controls, with fewer IALH UP evaluations.

6. ARBITRARY CNF. The m-family identity holds for every F and every M. The cost is mu(M), the number of maximal satisfiable subfamilies. The general obstruction is exactly that nothing bounds mu along any elimination sequence.
missing_theorem:
MT-A (should be provable; needs an independent proof and a Lean lemma): the two-family projection identity and witness lift of section 2, its m-family version, the gate-based node bound, and the STAR lattice lemma.

MT-B (open): module closure. Given F and a seed pair, either find in polynomial time a gated two-family module containing it or certify that none exists. A sufficient structural statement would be that syntactic two-family modules are closed under union of overlapping modules. I recall this holding for monotone clutters in the modular-decomposition literature, but I have not verified it and mixed polarity may break it. Without MT-B only fixed arity t is polynomial.

MT-C (not conjectured): an all-CNF bound. It would need either polynomial v5 leaf work on every CNF with no gated module, or a polynomial bound on the sum of mu(M_i) along some elimination sequence. I know no reason for either. Pigeonhole and random 3-CNF appear to have no gated modules.
self_attack:
1. This is functional (Ashenhurst-type) decomposition used as block DP with one definition variable. It is a restricted structural rule, and Neon58 already has short resolution refutations, so success there says nothing about hard inputs.
2. Brittle: the families must match exactly. One extra or missing clause creates a third family. The m-family form costs mu(M), which can be exponential in m. The drop-minority variant is UNSAT-only and heuristic.
3. Inert on pigeonhole, so the measured h=4 and h=5 IALH cost is untouched except by STAR, whose saving is a constant factor per window at best.
4. The size gate bounds the factoring overhead only. Leaf search stays potentially exponential.
5. Discovery above fixed arity is unproved. The 10-variable whole-side module in Neon58 is reached only through iterated arity-2 merges, and a family with large prime gates would defeat that.
6. Hand-trace risk: I counted contexts for {17,18} by reasoning, not enumeration. Canon/subsumption between merges could change families, though I expect it only to help.
7. Any local SAT answer of UNKNOWN must abort the rule. Syntactic family equality is sound but misses semantically equal families.
8. I cannot compare STAR with the 00069 full-lattice shortcut beyond its summary, so the two may overlap; the part I can claim as distinct is skipping the UP runs.
mechanism_signature: MODULE-SPLIT: context-grouped two-family projection EXISTS x_M F = R ^ [s12 v s1*Phi2 v s2*Phi1 v Phi1*Phi2], with one fresh selector, witness lift, a literal-count size gate and local-table certificates. It unifies OR/AND twins, XOR pairs and t-ary gates, and needs no dualization. Also STAR, an exact IALH window skip from a surviving Hamming star, and mu(M), the maximal-satisfiable-subfamily count, as the stated general obstruction.
delta_from_prior: Compared with the summaries I have: 00066 used rectangle definitions, 00068 used monotone dualization, and 00069 gave TWIN at arity 2 with arity-t modules left open. New here: (1) an exact arity-t rule with mixed polarity whose side condition is a local SAT call rather than a duality check, covering TWIN and arity-2 XOR as cases; (2) the m-family identity, which names mu(M) as the precise cost for arbitrary extras; (3) a size gate giving a linear node bound for the factoring overhead; (4) a hand trace refuting the raw 20-variable Neon58 in 15 merges without BLQ; (5) a pigeonhole negative control; (6) the STAR domination lemma for IALH work.
